title: Clean up without letting a cleanup failure mask the real one

blocks.text: If the `try` block throws and the `finally` block throws too, the exception from `finally` is the one that propagates, and the original is lost. The page's remedy: keep the original, and when the `finally` block has to throw, set the original as the new exception's cause with `initCause()`.
Write `Cleanup.run(Runnable work, Runnable cleanup)`. It runs `work`, then always runs `cleanup`.
Both are `RuntimeException`s, and a cleanup's exception is created without a cause of its own, so `initCause` may be called on it once.

cases.says: It runs the work, then the cleanup.
When the work fails, the cleanup still runs and the work's failure reaches the caller.
When both fail, the cleanup's exception is thrown with the work's exception as its cause instead of silently replacing it.
When only the cleanup fails, its exception still reaches the caller, with no cause attached.
The work's exception is attached as the cause with initCause, not added as suppressed.

concepts: An exception thrown from finally replaces the one from try, so the original is kept by setting it as the new exception's cause.
